summary.headline: Q2 FY27 disbursements fell to INR2,375 crore as Project Tejas IT migration hit branches; FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore held.
summary.overview: Can Fin Homes completed the full go-live of Project Tejas (IT transformation) across all branches, with the final ~93 old branches and new branches moving live from 1 October 2026. Disbursements for the quarter were INR2,375 crore, net of about INR29 crore of NHB-mandated cancellation netting, and management attributed the shortfall to one-time migration and process changes plus a Telangana Section 22 verification issue. Management held FY27 disbursement guidance of INR13,000 crore and AUM growth of 13-14%, and guided FY28 disbursement of INR16,000 crore with 15%+ AUM growth. Prepayments eased to INR1,795 crore from INR1,857 crore in Q1, and the company passed on a 10 bps housing rate hike effective 8 October 2026.

segments.name: Branches live on new system (Project Tejas)
segments.commentary: Rollout in phases: 11 branches in July (5 old, 6 new), 89 in August (75 old, 14 new), 77 old in September and 98 in October (93 old plus 5 new). Disbursements at branches during their go-live month dropped about 70-75%, recovering to 80-90% of prior run-rate the following month.

segments.name: Branches not yet migrated (93-branch cohort)
segments.commentary: Average monthly disbursement was INR435 crore in Q1 and rose to INR454, INR458, INR424 and INR481 crore in the months of July-September per management's slide 20 data (management's figures; not independently verified).

segments.name: Sales team channel
segments.commentary: Sales team headcount about 90 now, targeted at 150 by year-end and 250 in FY28; management expects INR1,500-1,600 crore from sales in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1.

segments.name: Karnataka
segments.commentary: Disbursement has stabilised at INR230-250 crore per period, per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 disbursement guidance held at INR13,000 crore (20%+ growth over INR10,500 crore in FY26); Q3 target about INR3,500 crore with the shortfall to be recovered in Q4.
FY27 AUM growth guidance of 13-14%, closer to 14%; management said the 15% AUM growth figure for FY28 is a resultant of disbursement and rundown.
FY28 disbursement internal target INR16,000 crore (about 22% growth), implying 15%+ AUM growth, closer to 15.5%.

Spread and NIM guidance of 2.75% and 3.75% maintained; management said it will pass through rate hikes, with about 12-13 bps of liability cost increase on the full book from the 25 bps repo hike and 10 bps passed on so far.
FY27 credit cost guidance of 10 bps maintained; gross NPA expected to fall in H2.
Plans to draw NHB refinance earlier, from Q3 if sanctions are higher, to benefit from lower rates; exploring an additional refinance limit.
capex_capacity: Project Tejas fully live: LOS and LMS live across all branches as of 1 October 2026; modules including risk, ALM, borrowings (by September 2025 onward) and deposits/DMS (January) implemented per management.
25 of 28 branches planned for FY27 are already operational with staff; these are expected to contribute in Q3 and Q4.
Branch expansion: about 12 branches added in UP in the last year, per management.
About 129 staff who were deployed on the IT project are being redeployed to branches and departments, with some support retained for 1-2 months.
demand_pricing: Management said underlying demand is robust with no change, and attributed the Q2 shortfall to process changes (about 8-10 additional OTPs per borrower and co-borrower), a 5-day post-month data handover lag, and a new Telangana Section 22 sub-registrar verification requirement.
Housing loan rate raised by 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 (new customers from 12 October); about 87% of floating book is on quarterly reset, about 12-13% on annual reset.
Management expects a 25 bps repo hike to translate into about 12-13 bps on the book, with plans to pass on about 15 bps next time.

Prepayment rate was about 15.5-16% historically and about 17-17.5% recently; management said a 100 bps rise could narrow the rate gap by around 60 bps, reducing prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.
Higher-ticket (INR30 lakh+) loans have grown, and the company is also looking at AHF-linked INR15-25 lakh loans as NHB AHF share rises.
PMAY 2.0 uptake described as slow relative to CLSS-1, with limited presence in the high-need states (Odisha, Bengal, Bihar, UP).
Management said the sales team contributed INR560 crore in H1 FY27 and targets about 20% of disbursement from sales in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Why did the liquidity coverage ratio rise well above the 100% regulatory minimum, and what is a steady level?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to lower short-term borrowings, now about 12% of borrowings versus 26-27% in March 2023, plus smaller bulk borrowings. LCR range cited as 135% to 250%; HQLA held at roughly INR2,300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Does a rising rate cycle affect home loan demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a 25-50 bps move is a non-event for demand because EMI impact is limited on 15-year tenors. Rates of 7.15-8% are among the lowest seen, so customer behaviour is not expected to change much.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk to FY27 disbursement target from the South monsoon or drought, and to asset quality?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is early to assess; drought has been declared in parts of Maharashtra and Karnataka, but the company lends mainly in Tier 1-2 areas. If industry slows, it could hit disbursement, and it may use LAP or construction top-ups as short-term levers.

qa_highlights.question: How will operational efficiency from Project Tejas play out in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited manual processes now automated, native AI features, auto form filling, and a digital sourcing channel expected to reach about 10% of business. Sales headcount to rise from about 90 to 150 this year without adding branch staff.

qa_highlights.question: What is the rate pass-through and prepayment outlook after the repo hike?
qa_highlights.answer: Housing rates rose 10 bps effective 8 October 2026 against a 25 bps repo hike, which translates to about 12-13 bps on the book. Management said a 100 bps rise could cut the rate gap by about 60 bps and reduce prepayment and rundown by about INR400 crore.

qa_highlights.question: How reset timing works for bank borrowings and the loan book, and whether spread is at risk in a rising cycle?
qa_highlights.answer: Repo-linked bank borrowings reprice from 1 November; T-bill-linked ones reset quarterly. About 87% of the floating book is on quarterly reset and 12-13% on annual, with roughly one-third repricing each on 1 November, 1 December and 1 January. Management said it will pass on hikes to protect spread and NIM.

qa_highlights.question: How confident is management in the H2 disbursement ramp (about INR3,500 crore per quarter) and the FY28 AUM outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 was INR2,600 crore against a planned INR2,500 crore, so the INR100 crore buffer was used; Q3 target is INR3,500 crore with about INR400 crore shortfall recovered in Q4. FY28 disbursement target of INR16,000 crore implies AUM growth of about 15-15.5%, with 15% described as a resultant figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is the productivity ramp for new branches and the pipeline status?
qa_highlights.answer: New branches take about 18 months (range 18-24) to reach 5 cases per staff per month. Management said sanctioned-but-not-disbursed rose about INR118 crore quarter on quarter, and that some pipeline was lost during the migration.

risks_watch: Q3 disbursement delivery against the INR3,500 crore target, and whether the INR400 crore shortfall is recovered in Q4 as guided.
Spread and NIM protection: liability cost rising about 12-13 bps on the full book against 10 bps passed on so far; management plans a next hike of about 15 bps.
Asset quality: SMA-0 uptick attributed to a daily versus month-end overdue computation change; gross NPA is expected to fall in H2 and credit cost is guided at 10 bps against about 9 bps in Q2.
Monsoon and drought risk to construction activity and demand in Maharashtra and Karnataka, plus Telangana Section 22 verification delays.
Sales channel ramp from about 90 to 150 staff (and 250 in FY28) to deliver INR1,500-1,600 crore in FY27 versus INR560 crore in H1, and the digital channel target of 10%.
Liability mix: NCD pricing around 8.3-8.35% versus bank term loans at about 7.65%, and special-rate T-bill-linked borrowings that reset at varying times.
Prepayment trend (INR1,795 crore in Q2 versus INR1,857 crore in Q1) after the housing rate hike, and the NHB refinance draw (INR1,350 crore sanctioned, expected at about 6.6-6.7%).
key_quotes: The month in which the implementation has happened, the disbursements, they have dropped in that particular branches by about 70% to 75%, and then the next month, again, it pushes back and it comes back to almost 80% -90% of the old disbursement.

Basically, in terms of the demand or in terms of the business per se, there has been no change, but for the impact of the IT transformation, which is mainly on account of the understanding, or rather the change in the flow, the additional processes that have been incorporated.
We will be looking at a 20% plus growth in terms of the disbursement, which consequently should become a 13%- 14% AUM growth this year and a 15% plus AUM growth in the next year.
Basically, our endeavor will be to ensure that our NIM and spread and NIM stays protected.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the full-year guidance and long-term benefit of Project Tejas, while openly attributing the Q2 shortfall to one-time migration issues. Management was more hedged on the Telangana verification issue and monsoon risk ("it's a little early"), and it was evasive on the exact timing of the sales ramp and branch productivity.
